### 🔹 Example in Python (OpenCV + OpenAI)

```python
import cv2
import base64
import requests
from openai import OpenAI
import io
from PIL import Image

client = OpenAI()

# Capture webcam
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)

while True:
    ret, frame = cap.read()
    if not ret:
        break

    # Show webcam feed
    cv2.imshow("Webcam", frame)

    # Convert frame to base64 (JPEG)
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode('.jpg', frame)
    b64_img = base64.b64encode(buffer).decode("utf-8")

    # Send every 2 seconds (avoid spamming API)
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4.1",
        messages=[
            {"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the main object in this image briefly."},
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{b64_img}"}
            ]}
        ]
    )

    caption = response.choices[0].message["content"]
    print("AI says:", caption)

    # Press 'q' to quit
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

cap.release()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
```

import gradio as gr
import base64
from openai import OpenAI
import cv2

client = OpenAI()

def describe_frame(frame):

    _, buffer = cv2.imencode('.jpg', frame)
    b64_img = base64.b64encode(buffer).decode("utf-8")

    # Call OpenAI GPT-4.1 Vision API
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4.1",
        messages=[
            {"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the main object in this image briefly."},
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{b64_img}"}
            ]}
        ]

    return caption

# Gradio UI

    fn=describe_frame,
    inputs=gr.Image(source="webcam", streaming=True),
    outputs="text",

import gradio as gr
from transformers import BlipProcessor, BlipForConditionalGeneration
from PIL import Image
import cv2

# Load BLIP2 model
processor = BlipProcessor.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")
model = BlipForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")

def describe_frame(frame):
    image = Image.fromarray(frame)
    inputs = processor(image, return_tensors="pt")
    out = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=50)
    caption = processor.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)
    return caption

    outputs="text",
    live=True,
    title="Real-Time Object Describer (Free, BLIP2)",

)

## 🔹 Block 3: Caption Function
```python
def describe_image(img):
    # Convert the image into model input
    inputs = processor(img, return_tensors="pt")

    # Generate caption (beam search for better quality)
    out = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=80, num_beams=5)

    # Decode model output into human-readable text
    caption = processor.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

    return caption
```

### 🔎 Explanation
- `inputs = processor(img, return_tensors="pt")`  
  → Turns image into tensors the model can read (`pt` = PyTorch).  
- `model.generate(..., max_length=80, num_beams=5)`  
  → Generates a caption with up to 80 words, using **beam search (5 beams)** for better quality.  
- `processor.decode(...)`  
  → Converts the model’s token output into text.  
- `return caption`  
  → Returns the description string.

import numpy as np

# Decide compute device: GPU if available, otherwise CPU
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Load processor and model from Hugging Face
# This will download model weights the first time you run it
processor = BlipProcessor.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")
model = BlipForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")

# Move model to chosen device and set eval mode
model.to(device)
model.eval()

def describe_image(frame: np.ndarray) -> str:
    """
    Receive a webcam frame (numpy array), return a caption string.
    This function will be called by Gradio for each frame (or each input).
    """
    try:
        # Convert numpy array (H,W,3) to PIL Image
        image = Image.fromarray(frame.astype("uint8"), "RGB")

        # Prepare inputs for the model (returns dict of tensors)
        inputs = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")

        # Move tensors to same device as model
        inputs = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in inputs.items()}

        # Generate caption tokens (beam search for quality)
        output_ids = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=80, num_beams=5)

        # Decode token ids to text using the tokenizer inside the processor
        caption = processor.tokenizer.decode(output_ids[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

        return caption
    except Exception as e:
        # Return a friendly error message if something goes wrong
        return f"Error generating caption: {e}"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Build Gradio interface
    demo = gr.Interface(
        fn=describe_image,                         # fn called on each input
        inputs=gr.Image(source="webcam", streaming=True),  # webcam input (streaming)
        outputs="text",                            # display caption as text
        live=True,                                 # allow live updates
        title="Real-Time Object Describer (BLIP2)",
        description="Point your camera at objects and get live captions."
    )

    # Launch the app on 0.0.0.0 so it can be viewed from other hosts if needed.
    # PORT can be overridden by environment variable for deployment.
    demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 7860)))

- `WORKDIR /app` — working directory.  
- `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y git-lfs ...` — installs `git-lfs` in case HF model files utilize LFS. Cleans cache.  
- `COPY requirements.txt .` — copy dependency list.  
- `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt` — install Python dependencies.  
- `COPY . .` — copy the project files.  
- `ENV PORT=7860` — default port env var.  
- `EXPOSE 7860` — container listens on this port.  
- `CMD ["python", "app.py"]` — command to start the app.
